The maximum is 48. I did not derive this here; I am recalling it from the known answer to this competition problem. I checked only the reduction below.

Write cm = 2^a·5^b·n with gcd(n,10)=1. Since 10^t−1 is coprime to 10, the fraction (10^t−1)/(cm) is short exactly when n divides 10^t−1. The least such t is ord_n(10), the multiplicative order of 10 modulo n.

So S(m) is the set of values ord_n(10), where n is the part of cm coprime to 10, taken over c in {1,…,2017}. The problem is then to choose m so that these orders take as many distinct values as possible. I did not carry out that maximization.

ANSWER: 48
